was the event map played in the

rerun. Like other event maps, this map had a specialized wave structure with special enemies. Players started with a varying amount of cash, based on how many players there were in the match and the difficulty chosen. Triumphing the Easy difficulty did not grant any additional rewards, but it did unlock the Hard difficulty. Triumphing the Hard difficulty gives the
tower on the first triumph, and in the additional rewards after their countdown timers finished.

Cash was only gained if an enemy is killed, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gained was a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. It used a slightly different method of distributing cash between players, as enemies split their cash between players, regardless of how much damage the player dealt to it. If, in a duo, one player did all the damage to an enemy, both players would receive 50% of the cash the enemy would normally give in solo. This means that in solo, you received 100% of the cash when an enemy is killed, or it was damaged enough. With each additional player, this was reduced to 50% in duo, 33% in trio and 25% in quad. If it was a decimal, it gets rounded up or down depending on the decimal value. If it was at least 0.5, it got rounded up. If it was less than 0.5, it got rounded down. For example, the

was a giant bathroom located in the duck realm, with the actual map taking place on top of a large countertop. The countertop had multiple wooden blocks, used to create various objects. There were also multiple huge versions of regular items, such as cups, brushes, band aids, nail clippers, playing cards, potted plants, scissors and toothbrushes. Outside the countertop, there was also a giant toilet, bathtub, door, washing machine and shelf. On the ground, there was a giant fortress with multiple wooden halls leading to the countertop. In the fortress,
The path started at two giant wooden halls and ended at a small house built out of blocks. There were two paths in Easy and four in Hard.

Loadouts could be only selected in the Easy difficulty. Alongside these preset options, players could opt to use the player's current loadout as the first choice. However, if one's loadout contained no towers, this option would be unavailable.
A loadout that prides itself in air superiority and locking down areas.
A defensive loadout specialized at sending units and deploying traps.
